pages.description: An easy way for Armed Forces personnel or their families to let IRS know they're in a combat zone.
pages.text: Notifying the IRS by Email about Combat Zone Service | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Notifying the IRS by Email about Combat Zone Service More In News Working Families Tax Cuts News releases Tax relief in disaster situations Topics in the news Fact sheets IRS statements and announcements IRS Tax Tips IRS guidance Media center Tax articles to share Posters to share Working with the Department of Defense, the Internal Revenue Service identifies taxpayers who are serving in a combat zone to suspend compliance actions, such as audits or enforced collections, until 180 days after the taxpayer has left the zone. Taxpayers, including civilian taxpayers working with U.S. Armed Forces, qualifying for such combat zone relief may also notify the IRS directly of their status through combatzone@irs.gov . They should provide their name, stateside address, date of birth, and the date of deployment to the combat zone. Taxpayers should also include any official document that indicates their area or military operation. Civilians usually provide a Letter of Authorization or a letter from their employer. However, letters from the military that state the taxpayer served in a tax-free zone or Combat Zone Tax Exclusion (CZTE) area are acceptable. Do not include any Social Security numbers in an email. The taxpayer, taxpayer's spouse, or an authorized agent or representative may make this notification. The IRS cannot provide tax account information by email. pages.text: Nvidia dismisses campaign to bring back Jensen Huang as Trump backs effort Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex boss 10 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Michael Race and Osmond Chia , Business reporters Getty Images Donald Trump greeting Jensen Huang in September this year Nvidia has dismissed a campaign calling for the company's co-founder Jensen Huang to be handed back his job as allies, including US President Donald Trump, supported the effort. Trump said on Monday that he "would certainly not mind" if Huang was reinstated, joining a list of supporters including SpaceX's Elon Musk who are backing a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign. But the BBC has been told the board of the AI chip giant is not interested in reinstating him after he resigned last week following revelations he had two affairs , including one that involved a suspected Chinese spy. The same day, the White House also said it will further restrict China's access to AI chips from firms like Nvidia. The reported affairs created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a central company in AI and the US battle against China for dominance. Since Huang's departure, more than 175,000 people have signed an open letter calling for the board to reinstate the tech billionaire while an ongoing internal probe is conducted. For Beijing, the former Nvidia CEO's dramatic fall is a major challenge - and not just because of claims that a Chinese spy may have honey-trapped Huang, one of the artificial intelligence industry's most influential figures. Rather, the allegations surrounding Huang and his affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang are turning into a new flashpoint in an already fragile US-China relationship. US intelligence reports claim she had ties to Beijing's intelligence apparatus - in particular the Ministry of State Security, China's main civilian spy agency. The claim remains unproven, but it has already reignited debate in Washington over exports of advanced chips to China and whether the Trump administration has been too willing to ease restrictions. pages.text: Nvidia: How the Jensen Huang scandal exposed a headache for business-friendly Singapore Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore 3 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Tessa Wong and Osmond Chia , Singapore Getty Images A major scandal involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy based in Singapore has cast a spotlight on the city-state's success as a global chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade. On Thursday, Huang stepped down from the US chip giant after admitting he had an affair. He was reportedly involved with a woman named Alice Huang, who ran Singaporean data centre company Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's chips. For decades, Singapore has painstakingly cultivated a reputation as an open, business-friendly economy offering easy access to both the US and Chinese markets. With the AI boom, it has become a major hub for the trade of high-end semiconductor chips in recent years. Singapore was the second-largest billing centre globally last year for Nvidia, accounting for nearly a fifth of what the US chip giant earns. But notably, less than 1% of its earnings were for chips that actually entered Singapore, as the island acts as a hub for many Asian companies to place orders and send them elsewhere. It describes occupations in terms of the knowledge, skills, and abilities required as well as how the work is performed in terms of tasks, work activities, and other descriptors. O*NET database Content Model Every occupation requires a different mix of knowledge, skills, and abilities, and is performed using a variety of activities and tasks. These distinguishing characteristics, or "descriptors", of an occupation are collected, codified, and described by the O*NET Content Model . This hierarchical model starts with six domains (or categories), describing the day-to-day aspects of the job and the qualifications and interests of the typical worker. The model includes nearly 277 descriptors collected by the O*NET program, along with other occupational data collected by other federal agencies such as the Bureau of Labor Statistics . Data Collection Real-world information The Data Collection program brings the Content Model frameworks to life with results from the working public. The O*NET database is collected and updated through ongoing surveys of workers in each occupation supplemented in some cases by occupation experts. pages.text: Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral La Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral (Office of Labor-Management Standards, u OLMS, por sus siglas en inglés) pertenece al Departamento de Trabajo de los Estados Unidos y es responsable de administrar y aplicar la mayoría de las disposiciones de la Ley de Notificación y Divulgación Gestión Laboral (Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act, o LMRDA, por sus siglas en inglés). Dicha ley fue adoptada con el fin de garantizar normas básicas de democracia y responsabilidad fiscal en las organizaciones laborales del sector privado. Los sindicatos que representan a los empleados del Correo Postal de los Estados Unidos también se hallan sujetos a la LMRDA. Los sindicatos de empleados federales se hallan sujetos a normas similares conforme a la Ley de Reforma del Servicio Civil de 1978 (Civil Service Reform Act, o CSRA, por sus siglas in inglés) y a la Ley del Servicio Exterior de 1980. La OLMS anima a que los oficiales y los miembros del sindicato, así como otros individuos afectados por la LMRDA, se pongan en contacto con la agencia para discutir de problemas, presenten quejas u obtengan información sobre la LMRDA. Además, la OLMS fomenta la conformidad voluntaria con la LMRDA al informar a oficiales del sindicato y a otros individuos de sus responsabilidades y al animar a los miembros del sindicato a que ejerzan sus derechos. By accessing the OLMS EFS, you can also obtain, work on, or sign and submit an LM form. For more information on registering with EFS, see the Registration Help page . pages.text: One thing Hollywood gets right about Ancient Rome | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE One thing Hollywood gets right about Ancient Rome Gladiators really were sex symbols—just not in the way one might expect. Gladiators were ancient Roman sex symbols Rebecca Hale, National Geographic By Harry Sidebottom Published July 24, 2026 Hollywood is often criticized for getting history wrong, rarely more so than in films about Rome . One could take issue with the lack of color, whether in the robes that clothe posh-sounding British actors or the statues and other works in marble stripped of their polychromy. In arguably the most famous movie about Rome, Gladiator , inaccuracies abound, from puzzling choices in how the gladiators are armed to the tigers released to endanger the combatants. Credulity is strained even further in the sequel when a naval fight is recreated in the Colosseum (which could not be flooded by the period in which the film is set) and great white sharks devour those who fall into the water. The heights of physical impossibility are reached when a gladiator rides a rhinoceros, complete with saddle and stirrups, into the arena. But there is one thing Hollywood gets right. As the graffiti etched into barracks in Pompeii capture, gladiators saw themselves as sex symbols. It allows different vendors to work together, encouraging competition, driving new ideas, and creating smarter, more efficient networks. Open RAN is a step toward more reliable wireless communications. Next generation RANs are characterized by the disaggregation of the network elements and the use of intelligent controllers to manage the increased complexity of radio technologies and network deployments. The disaggregation of the network elements to create an Open RAN that allows the equipment from different vendors to communicate requires well-defined, standardized interfaces. Furthermore, the increased complexity of the network and the need for real-time control forces the network operators to investigate automated solutions based on Machine Learning (ML) algorithms. Reports Online Sources Cited in Opinions Media Files Cited in Opinions Case Citation Finder Opinions The term “opinions” as used on this website refers to several types of writing by the Justices. The most well-known opinions are those released or announced in cases in which the Court has heard oral argument. Each opinion sets out the Court’s judgment and its reasoning and may include the majority or principal opinion as well as any concurring or dissenting opinions. All opinions in a single case are published together and are prefaced by a syllabus prepared by the Reporter of Decisions that summarizes the Court’s decision. The Justice who authors the majority or principal opinion often will summarize the opinion from the bench during a Court session. The Court may also dispose of cases in per curiam opinions, which do not identify the author. These cases frequently resolve cases summarily, often without oral argument. But per curiam opinions have sometimes been issued in argued cases. In-chambers opinions are written by an individual Justice to dispose of an application by a party for interim relief, e.g. , for a stay of the judgment of the court below, for vacation of a stay, or for a temporary injunction. The arguments are an opportunity for the Justices to ask questions directly of the attorneys representing the parties to the case, and for the attorneys to highlight arguments that they view as particularly important. Arguments are generally scheduled on specified Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday mornings beginning on the first Monday in October, and continuing through the end of April. Typically, the Court holds two arguments each day beginning at 10:00 a.m. The days on which arguments are held are identified on the Court’s yearly calendar . The specific cases to be argued each day, and the attorneys scheduled to argue them, are identified on hearing lists for each session and on the day call for each argument session. The Court is currently conducting a pilot program in which members of the public may apply for Courtroom seating through an online lottery . During this pilot program, Courtroom seating will also be available to the public on a first-come, first-seated basis. An audio feed of the argument is live-streamed on the Court's website, and the Court posts the audio later in the day. The public land found in eastern Oregon is characterized by large swaths of basin and range topography. These dramatic, semi-arid landscapes provide a wide variety of recreation and commercial opportunities while also proving habitat for a diverse array of fish and wildlife species. In Washington, the BLM lands are found predominantly east of the Cascade Mountain Range but can be visited as far west as the San Juan Islands.
